construction_markdown:
No unconditional inner code was found. The strongest concrete handoff is the following deterministic reduction.

Assume an explicit binary code `U=[8192,16,4092]₂` with ordered generator rows `u₁,…,u₁₆`. Define

`B₀={(u,u+t·1₈₁₉₂):u∈U, t∈F₂}` and `B₁=span{b}`, where `b=(0,1₈₁₉₂)`.

Then `dim(B₀)=17`, `dim(B₁)=1`, `wt(b)=8192`, and every word of `B₀\B₁` has weight at least 8184: for `t=0` its weight is `2wt(u)≥8184`, while for `t=1` its weight is exactly 8192. Thus this is the exceptional-line flag required by `composition-r002-01`.

For completeness, the resulting conditional target code can be specified directly. Let `F=F₂[Z]/(Z¹⁶+Z⁵+Z³+Z²+1)`, order its 65536 elements by their 16-bit polynomial coordinates, and take the full-length Reed–Solomon evaluation code of polynomials of degree at most 64. It has parameters `[65536,65,65472]₍F₎`. Identify the polynomial basis of `F` with the ordered rows of `U`; write the induced linear isomorphism as `ψ:F→U`. For an outer word `(a_x)_{x∈F}`, encode block `x` as `(ψ(a_x),ψ(a_x))`, and optionally add `b` in every block. The binary dimension is `16·65+1=1041`, length is `65536·16384=2³⁰`, and the conditional distance is at least `min(8184·65472,8192·65536)=535822848>D`.

The unresolved object is exactly the symbolic, polynomial-time generator for `U`. It cannot be replaced by a lookup or exhaustive selector.

Its quotient words have weight at least 8184 and its distinguished word has weight 8192. With the deterministic `[65536,65,65472]` RS quotient outer code and a repeated bottom bit, this gives an explicit `[2³⁰,1041,≥535822848]₂` code. This is a one-dimension improvement over the durable 1040 construction, conditional only on the core `U`.

generator_matrix.algorithm: Conditional algorithm: take an explicit ordered `16×8192` generator `G_U`. Use `F=F₂[Z]/(Z¹⁶+Z⁵+Z³+Z²+1)` and list field elements by increasing 16-bit polynomial coordinate. For each of the 65 monomials and each of the 16 field-basis coefficients, evaluate the corresponding monomial at all 65536 field elements. At evaluation value `a`, express `a` in the fixed basis, multiply that 16-bit vector by `G_U` to obtain `ψ(a)`, and output the 16384-bit block `(ψ(a),ψ(a))`. These are 1040 rows. Output one final row consisting of 65536 copies of `(0₈₁₉₂,1₈₁₉₂)`. No unconditional execution is claimed because `G_U` is missing.
generator_matrix.runtime_bound: Conditional on the core generator, fewer than `1040·65536·(64·16²+16·8192)+1041n < 2¹⁵n < n²` bit operations at `n=2³⁰`.
generator_matrix.runtime_proof: Horner evaluation of each degree-at-most-64 monomial row costs at most `64·16²` bit operations per field point under schoolbook fixed-degree arithmetic. Forming a block from the 16 core rows costs at most `16·8192` bit operations, and writing the output costs `1041n`. Substitution of the fixed parameters gives the displayed bound. Thus the reduction preserves explicit polynomial-time full-matrix generation, but only after an explicit `G_U` is supplied.

proof_markdown:
### Residual lemma and refined finite bounds

Let `N₂(k,d)` denote the minimum length of a binary linear code of dimension `k` and distance at least `d`. If `c` is a minimum word of weight `d` in a `[N,k,d]₂` code, puncture on its support. The kernel is exactly `<c>`: a second independent kernel word would split the support of `c` into two nonzero codewords, one of weight at most `d/2<d`. For any other word, comparing it with its sum with `c` shows that its weight outside `supp(c)` is at least `ceil(d/2)`. Therefore

`N₂(k,d) ≥ d + N₂(k-1,ceil(d/2))`.

The exact theorem `N₂(9,32)=70` from [Bouyukliev–Guritman–Vavrek](https://www.moi.math.bas.bg/moiuser/~iliya/pdf_site/getPDFbgv.pdf) now gives

`N₂(16,4094)≥4094+2047+1024+512+256+128+64+70=8195`,

`N₂(16,4095)≥4095+2048+1024+512+256+128+64+70=8197`,

and hence `N₂(17,8188)≥16383` and `N₂(17,8189)≥16386`.

### Forced full-gateway residuals

Suppose `C=[16384,17,≥8188]₂`. The last bound forces its actual minimum to be 8188. Residualizing a minimum word gives `[8196,16,≥4094]`; its actual minimum is 4094 because a value at least 4095 would require length 8197. The next residual is `[4102,15,≥2047]`. Griesmer gives `g(15,2049)=4110`, so its minimum is 2047 or 2048.

If it is 2048, repeated residualization forces

`[4102,15,2048]→[2054,14,1024]→[1030,13,512]→[518,12,256]→[262,11,128]→[134,10,64]→[70,9,32]`.

If it is 2047, it forces

`[4102,15,2047]→[2055,14,1024]→[1031,13,512]→[519,12,256]→[263,11,128]→[135,10,64]→[71,9,32]`.

Exactness at successive stages follows from `g(14,1025)=2061`, `g(13,513)=1036`, `g(12,257)=523`, `g(11,129)=266`, `g(10,65)=137`, and `g(9,33)=72`.

### The 8192-core reduction

Suppose `U=[8192,16,4092]₂`. The flag construction in `construction_markdown` is linear and has dimension 17 because `(0,1)` is independent of all `(u,u)`. Its weight calculation proves the claimed flag parameters. Concatenating its 16-dimensional quotient with the `[65536,65,65472]` full-field RS code and repeating the bottom line gives dimension `16·65+1=1041`. A nonzero quotient outer word has at least 65472 nonzero blocks, each of weight at least 8184 even after adding the bottom word. A pure bottom word has weight `8192·65536`. This proves the conditional target distance.

The core itself is also defect-one. The recurrence gives `N₂(16,4092)≥8191` and `N₂(16,4093)≥8194`, so its actual minimum would be 4092. Its residual is exactly `[4100,15,2046]`, since `N₂(15,2047)≥4101`. The next residual has parameters `[2054,14,d]` with `d∈{1023,1024}`. The `d=1024` branch continues through lengths `1030,518,262,134,70`; the `d=1023` branch continues through `1031,519,263,135,71`, with the same dimensions and distances as the full-gateway branches above.

### Structured-family exclusions

For a one-step Plotkin code `P(A,V)={(a,a+v)}` of half-length `m`, target distance implies `d(V)` is at least the full target distance and `d(A)` at least half of it. Every binary linear code of dimension at least two and length `m` has distance at most `2m/3`: in a two-dimensional subcode, the three nonzero words have total weight at most `2m`. Thus a full gateway would have `dim(V)≤1` and `dim(A)≥16`, producing a forbidden `[8192,16,≥4094]` subcode. Likewise a core would produce a forbidden `[4096,15,≥2046]` subcode. Hence neither is one-step Plotkin.

For binary cyclic length `N=2ˢ`, `Xᴺ-1=(X+1)ᴺ`, and every cyclic code is generated by a power of `X+1`. A code of dimension at least 16 contains `(X+1)^(N-16)`. Lucas' theorem gives its coefficient weight `2^popcount(N-16)=2^(s-4)`, namely 1024 for `s=14` and 512 for `s=13`. Both are far below the required distances.

Finally, let `μ:F₂ʳ→Z≥0` be the generator-column multiplicity and `S(a)=Σ_x μ(x)(-1)^(a·x)`. Minimum distance is equivalent to an upper bound on every nontrivial `S(a)`. If `μ(x)=μ(x+h)` for nonzero `h`, collapse the pairs modulo `<h>`. For every nonzero quotient character, `S(a)=2T(a)`. In the full gateway `S(a)≤8`, so the quotient has length 8192, dimension 16, and distance at least `(8192-4)/2=4094`, contradicting `N₂(16,4094)≥8195`. Applied to the core, the quotient would be `[4096,15,≥2046]`, contradicting `N₂(15,2046)≥4099`. Thus both column multisets must be additively aperiodic.

proof_steps.proof: The cited paper proves nonexistence at length 69 and constructs length 70.
Puncturing outside a minimum word has kernel exactly its span; comparing `x` and `x+c` gives residual distance at least `ceil(d/2)`.
The refined lower bounds force exact minima 8188 and 4094. The next minimum is 2047 or 2048, after which the displayed Griesmer inequalities force every successive value.

proof_steps.proof: Quotienting any nonzero translation period halves the Walsh cap and produces a forbidden `[8192,16,4094]` or `[4096,15,2046]` code.
proof_steps.statement: Every viable full gateway or 8192-core generator-column multiset has trivial additive translation stabilizer.

proof_steps.proof: Deleting disjoint nonzero subspaces of dimensions `u_i` from the 16-dimensional simplex would require `Σ(2^u_i-1)=57343`. The usual distance certificate requires `Σ2^u_i≤57352`, hence at most nine subspaces. Pairwise trivial intersection permits at most one dimension at least nine, so the sum is at most `2^15+8·2^8=34816`, a contradiction.
proof_steps.statement: The standard pairwise-disjoint whole-subspace Solomon–Stiffler deletion certificate cannot produce the 8192-core.

theorem_statement: Using the exact finite result `N₂(9,32)=70`, a full `[16384,17,8188]₂` gateway and a hypothetical `[8192,16,4092]₂` exceptional-line core each have one of two forced residual towers ending at `[134,10,64]→[70,9,32]` or `[135,10,64]→[71,9,32]`. Both inner objects are excluded from one-step Plotkin, binary cyclic, and additively periodic column-multiset families. Conversely, any deterministic polynomial-time `[8192,16,4092]₂` core yields a completely specified conditional `[2³⁰,1041,≥535822848]₂` construction.
